data.title: Lockheed unveils next-gen Patriot interceptor to defend against hypersonic threats
data.description:
Lockheed Martin (LMT) on Friday unveiled its new PAC-3 Edge missile interceptor, which it said will will add "a revolutionary defensive capability" against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, as the U.S. military seeks to strengthen its capabilities to counter emerging aerial threats.

Lockheed (LMT) said PAC-3 Edge incorporates a new seeker, upgraded flight controls, and a ​multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman (NOC), enhancing ​the interceptor's ability to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic missiles, ‌and providing greater speed and maneuverability, allowing it to fly at higher altitudes and longer distances than other PAC-3 missiles.

The new interceptor is part of the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor program currently in competition, and builds on Lockheed's (LMT) PAC-3 MSE, which has been used extensively to defend against missile attacks in Ukraine and Iran.

"The cost of this would be about that of the existing PAC-3 MSE," Tim Cahill, Lockheed (LMT) president of missiles and ​fire control Tim Cahill ⁠told Reuters. "At full production, the annual rate would be about 2,000 ​units a year, comparable with PAC-3 MSE."

Lockheed (LMT) said it will advance development and begin testing PAC-3 Edge in 2027 to prepare for rapid deployment by 2031.

data.title: Alignment Healthcare downgraded at BofA after CMS Star Rating for MA contract
data.description:
BofA Securities on Friday downgraded Alignment Healthcare (ALHC) to Neutral from Buy after CMS lowered its Star Rating for one of its major California Medicare Advantage contracts to 3.5 stars from 4.

The bank lowered its price target to $9 from $25 (~19% upside based on the Oct. 9 close).

BofA noted that Alignment Healthcare went from having all of its members in plans with at least 4 stars to just 25%. The important California contract, H3815, is responsible for 75% of the managed care company's MA membership.

As a result, the contracts with a rating of below 4 stars won't eligible for bonus payment from CMS, which "potentially [makes] it more
difficult to expand profitably into new markets," analyst Kevin Fischbeck said.

"However, there is a potential silver lining, in that if the company can move up its star rating on that one contract, there will be a meaningful lift to profitability in 2029, he added. "We see this as real potential, but visibility remains low and the binary nature of the event likely means that the ALHC stock will trade at a discount to its historical average until we see improvement."

Alignment Healthcare closed down ~13%.

data.title: Gold snaps two-week losing streak; some analysts say may have found bottom
data.description:
Gold futures rose Friday to finish at one-week highs, ‌posting a weekly gain after back-to-back losses, supported by resilient investment demand despite rising U.S. Treasury yields and a stronger dollar.

Elevated bond yields and persistent inflation pressures continue to keep a lid on gold prices, but analysts noted that investors continue to see value in the market as dips continue to be bought.

Despite the risks, this week's price action suggests the gold market may have found its bottom, Forex.com market analyst Fawad Razaqzada said in a note.

"Gold investors are largely seeing through risks of tighter monetary policy because of concerns that inflation may again overshoot due to high oil prices," Razaqzada wrote. "Precious metals are proving their worth as a hedge against inflation, with fiat currencies continuing to lose value across the world due to persistent price pressures. This is reflected in gold-backed ETFs continuing to receive inflows during the recent price decline."

High borrowing costs could ultimately support gold through two scenarios, according to Saxo Bank's Ole Hansen: an economic slowdown that drives yields lower and encourages monetary easing, or rising government debt servicing costs that prompt policy intervention and weaken confidence in monetary discipline.

"Neither outcome is inevitable, and further increases in real yields remain a near-term risk," Hansen said in a note. "Nevertheless, continued ETF accumulation suggests some investors are positioned for the potential consequences of elevated borrowing costs rather than simply responding to current interest-rate movements."

Gold ​gained this week because of "bargain hunting at the lows, as a floor has been building in the $4,000-region," ​StoneX head of market analysis Rhona O'Connell wrote. "It is arguable that a further Fed hike is already priced in but so is the expectation for continued official sector net purchases. Without any Black ​Swan event, I find it hard to see gold breaking convincingly higher."

This week, front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for October delivery gained 1.4% to $4,191.00/oz, its highest settlement value in a week, and front-month Comex October silver (XAGUSD:CUR) added 1.1% to $60.670/oz; on Friday, gold and silver rose 1.4% and 2.7%, respectively.

data.title: Integra LifeSciences prices $450M in 9.5% secured notes
data.description:
• Integra LifeSciences (IART) said it priced $450M in 9.5% senior secured notes due 2033, with the offering expected to close around Oct. 19.
  • Proceeds from the notes, combined with borrowings under new credit facilities, will be used to refinance existing credit facilities.
  • The new debt will have guarantees from the company’s wholly owned U.S. subsidiaries that back its existing secured credit facilities.

data.title: Gran Tierra Energy expects $315M cash from $1.33B business sale
data.description:
Gran Tierra Energy (GTE) announced on Friday that stockholders approved the sale of its Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses to Maurel & Prom for approximately $1.33B.

The company expects to receive ~$315M in net cash proceeds, including $250M at closing and $65M payable 364 days later.

The deal still requires regulatory approvals in Colombia and Ecuador, with closing targeted for December 31, 2026.

Moreover, it expects to be debt-free after the sale and plans to use part of the proceeds for a share repurchase, subject to completion of the sale and board approval.

On the market side, the GTE stock traded ~3% higher at ~$10.90 in the after-hours session.

data.title: Ruanyun Edai Technology receives Nasdaq minimum bid price notice
data.description:

data.title: NASA seeks commercial space station proposals
data.description:
NASA on Friday issued a final request for proposals to develop commercial space stations that could replace the International Space Station, advancing plans to shift low Earth orbit operations to private companies while maintaining a continuous U.S. presence in space.

The agency said proposals are due Dec. 8, with contract awards expected in spring 2027. NASA plans to select at least two contractors for initial development before holding a subsequent competition for final design, testing, certification and operational services.

The solicitation represents a potential opportunity for publicly traded aerospace companies, including Boeing (BA), Lockheed Martin (LMT), Northrop Grumman (NOC) and Redwire (RDW), as NASA moves toward purchasing commercial services rather than owning and operating its own orbital research facilities.

New revenue opportunities

NASA intends to award multiple firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts covering the development, certification and operation of commercial space stations. The agency is seeking companies capable of providing integrated destinations and transportation services for astronauts conducting research and technology development in low Earth orbit.

The initiative could create a longer-term market for spacecraft manufacturers, engineering contractors, suppliers of orbital infrastructure and companies providing transportation and logistics services. However, the solicitation does not guarantee contract awards or revenue for any particular company.

Among the publicly traded companies with potential exposure, Boeing (BA) has extensive experience building and supporting the ISS, while Lockheed (LMT) has been involved in commercial space station development through its work with Starlab Space. Northrop (NOC) has supported commercial station development efforts and supplies cargo transportation services to the ISS.

Redwire (RDW), which develops space infrastructure, microgravity research equipment and other orbital technologies, could benefit from demand for station components and research capabilities. Its opportunities may arise through subcontracting and equipment sales rather than serving as a prime station operator.

Private companies, including Axiom Space, Vast and Starlab Space, are also pursuing commercial orbital destinations. Their projects could generate additional business for publicly traded suppliers and transportation providers, depending on which teams ultimately receive NASA support.

Financially sustainable space

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman emphasized that commercial operators will need business models extending beyond government contracts, reflecting the agency's effort to establish a sustainable private market for orbital research and services.

"The opportunity is significant, but the economics ultimately have to work," Isaacman said.

The agency expects commercial stations to support scientific research, technology development, astronaut training and preparations for future missions to the Moon and Mars. NASA would become a customer of privately operated facilities rather than bearing the full cost of maintaining its own station.

The approach also introduces financial risks for participating companies. Fixed-price contracts can expose contractors to cost overruns, while the commercial market for private orbital research and manufacturing remains relatively unproven.

For investors, the December proposal deadline and expected spring 2027 awards will provide important milestones for assessing which companies may capture a share of NASA's future low Earth orbit spending. The eventual contract values, government funding commitments and ability of station operators to attract nongovernment customers will help determine whether commercial space stations become a meaningful source of revenue for the aerospace industry.

data.title: Star Bulk Carriers renews ATM agreements for up to $116.4M
data.description:
• Star Bulk Carriers (SBLK) said on Friday it renewed its existing ATM share sale arrangements after the shelf registration statement supporting the programs expired.

data.title: Hims & Hers Health climbs 10% amid recent volatile trading
data.description:
Shares of Hims & Hers Health (HIMS), a consumer-focused digital health and telehealth platform, rose 10% on Friday. The stock rose $2.86 to close at $30.92, rebounding from a 5% decline the previous session. The advance also came as volume reached 15.92 million shares, roughly 1.65 times the one-month average daily volume.

Shares have seen choppy trading lately, alternating gains and losses over the past six sessions.
